title: Soter Labs holds GovOps for all three Executor Agents simultaneously
content:
Reading the three Executor Agent stubs together reveals a concentration the individual documents do not surface:

| Executor Agent | Facilitator | GovOps |
|---|---|---|
| Amatsu (A.6.1.2.1) | Endgame Edge | **Soter Labs** |
| Ozone (A.6.1.2.2) | Redline Facilitation Group | **Soter Labs** |
| Core Council Executor Agent 1 (A.6.1.2.3) | JanSky | **Soter Labs** |

Facilitators are deliberately distinct — three different entities. GovOps is not: one entity holds it across all three.

That matters because the Facilitator/GovOps split is a separation-of-duties arrangement, and separation only delivers independence if both sides vary. With a common GovOps, any failure, capture or outage of that single entity propagates to every Executor Agent at once, and the three separate Facilitators provide no containment for it. Combined with the Artifacts being unspecified, there is currently no published constraint on how that shared role must be exercised.
description: A.6.1.2.1.2, A.6.1.2.2.2 and A.6.1.2.3.2 each name Soter Labs, concentrating operational governance of every Executor Agent in one entity while Facilitators stay separate.
